gen-dafont-joystix-noto-serif: Joystix is all arcade swagger, its widely tracked letters stamped out with stems barely heavier than the arms. Noto Serif is the literary one, with a prominent x-height and a gentle thick-and-thin rhythm running across each line.
gen-dafont-kg-happy-bitter: Cheerful, chunky handwriting with narrow lowercase openings leads the way. Bitter, a slab-serif, has a very large lowercase eye and a visible gap in each s, so long paragraphs feel grounded and unhurried.
gen-dafont-kg-happy-fs-literata: Youthful and chunky, with diagonals as stout as uprights. Literata, a text serif, has curved letters with wide, unclosed mouths, so shrinking KG Happy would pinch its tight lowercase while enlarging Literata would only show off its quiet thick-thin variation.
gen-dafont-kg-happy-inter: Bouncy, cheerful handwriting with a dominant x-height. Inter, a sans-serif, has big counters and a smooth, tube-like line, so it lets KG Happy's tighter letters stand out while the page stays open.
gen-dafont-kg-happy-roboto-slab: KG Happy is the youthful one, its handwritten strokes stout and its lowercase openings narrow. Roboto Slab, a slab-serif, is the precise one, with open throats on a, c, e and s and a middle zone that dominates each line.
gen-dafont-kingthings-exeter-fs-erode: Erode reads tall in the middle, with shallow ascenders and a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight. Kingthings Exeter brings the historical weight, and together with that text serif it is the traditional-meets-editorial mix that stands out most.
gen-dafont-klaudia-archivo: Klaudia's flowing pen-written letters all share one fixed stroke thickness, like a skeleton outline traced in a single nib. Archivo, a sans-serif, adds a commanding x-height and curves that open outward, and the mix feels casual and approachable at once.
gen-dafont-klaudia-clash-grotesk: Pen-written Klaudia keeps one fixed stroke thickness, with wide-set terminals on its s. Clash Grotesk, a sans-serif with no thick-and-thin modulation at all, is the pair's strongest quality, a clean and approachable partner made for brief reading.
gen-dafont-klaudia-fs-asap: Luxurious, with a casual hand and flowing pen-written letters. Asap, a sans, has c forms like open arcs and a body height nearly matching its capitals, so a long page reads readable and brisk.
gen-dafont-klaudia-fs-epilogue: Casual and flowing, Klaudia writes every letter with one fixed stroke thickness and wide-set terminals on its s. Epilogue, a plain sans, runs tall and wire-thin with curvy letters, so reading it feels contemporary and relaxed.
